checks.lead: Alexander V of Macedon (Greek: Ἀλέξανδρος Εʹ ὁ Μακεδών; died late 294 BC) was the second son of Cassander and Thessalonike of Macedon, who was a half-sister of Alexander the Great.  He ruled as king of Macedon along with his brother Antipater I from the autumn of 297 to autumn 294 BC.
